say.en: A variable is like a label stuck on a value in memory. The value might be a whole number, a decimal, some text or a list. Python must know which kind it is. How? In this lesson: Create variables with assignment.
Write comments.
Classify Python data types and identify mutable and immutable types.

body.en: A variable is a name that refers to a value stored in memory. It is created when we assign a value with =, for example marks = 85. Python decides the type from the value, and the same variable can later refer to a value of another type. A comment begins with # and is ignored by the interpreter; it explains the code to human readers. In Python everything is an object: each object has a unique identity, which id() returns, a type and a value.

points.en: *Comments* start with # and are not executed

body.en: Numbers: int (whole numbers such as −5 and 42), float (real numbers such as 3.14) and complex (such as 2 + 3j). bool has only True and False and is a subtype of int. Sequences: str (text in quotes), list (items in square brackets) and tuple (items in round brackets). A set holds unordered unique items in curly braces. None means no value. A dict (dictionary) maps keys to values. Lists, sets and dictionaries are mutable (their contents can change); int, float, complex, bool, str and tuple are immutable.

title.en: A variable is a box with a name

say.en: A computer remembers things in boxes. Each box has a name written on it, like score.
The equals sign means: put this in the box. Now the box called score holds 0.
A box holds one thing at a time. When we put 5 in, the old 0 is thrown out.
print(score) peeks in the box and shows what is there. The 5 stays in the box.

title.en: Use a box to make a new value

say.en: score = score + 1 means: take what is in score, add 1, and put the answer back. Now it holds 6.

title.en: Lots of boxes, lots of names

say.en: Programs use many boxes. They can hold words, numbers, or True and False. The name tells you which box is which.

goal.en: Store a number in a variable, change it, then add 1 to it.

explain.en: A variable is a box in the computer's memory with a name on it. The = sign means store: put the value on the right into the box on the left. Now score holds 5.

explain.en: In code, = does not mean is equal to. The computer works out the right side first (8 + 1 = 9), then stores the answer back in score. This is how games add points.

takeaway.en: A variable is a named box: = stores a new value in it (the old one is thrown away), and the right side is worked out first.
